original_text: Transport in Vertebrates All vertebrates have a closed circulatory system called a cardiovascular system Vertebrate heart: Atria of heart receive blood from general circulation Ventricles of heart pump blood out through blood vessels Vertebrate vessels: Arteries-Carry blood away from heart Thicker walls, to accommodate sudden influxes of blood from pump (high pressure) Arterioles Lead to capillaries Capillaries-Exchange materials with tissue fluid All cells within 60-80um of capillary bed Only 5% of organisms capillary beds open at one time Venules-Lead to veins Veins-Return blood to heart Thinner walls than arteries (lower blood pressure). Have valves
explanation: All vertebrates possess a closed circulatory system known as a cardiovascular system. The vertebrate heart consists of atria (which receive blood returning from circulation) and ventricles (which pump blood out). Vertebrate vessels include: 1) Arteries: carry blood away from the heart, possessing thick walls to handle the high pressure of pumped blood. 2) Arterioles: branches that lead to capillaries. 3) Capillaries: microscopic vessels where nutrient and gas exchange occurs; cells are within 60-80 $\mu m$ of a capillary bed, and only 5% of beds are open at one time. 4) Venules: collect blood from capillaries and lead to veins. 5) Veins: return blood to the heart, possessing thinner walls (due to lower pressure) and internal valves to prevent backflow.

questions.q: Why do arteries have thicker walls than veins?
opts: To allow for the passive diffusion of oxygen across their walls
To accommodate the high pressure and sudden influxes of pumped blood
To prevent the backflow of low-pressure blood
To store excess glucose as glycogen
questions.exp: Arteries must withstand the high pressure and surges of blood ejected directly from the heart, requiring thicker, more elastic walls than veins.

questions.q: What type of blood vessel is thin-walled and facilitates the exchange of materials, and how close are cells to them?
questions.exp: Capillaries are the sites of material exchange. All cells in the vertebrate body are located within 60-80 micrometers of a capillary bed.

questions.q: What structural feature in veins helps return low-pressure blood to the heart against gravity?
questions.exp: Veins contain one-way internal valves that prevent the backflow of blood, assisting its return to the heart under low pressure.
